title: N4 · Unit 9

lesson.title: A changed meeting room
lesson.description: Distinguish a passive event from a prepared state, report an interruption and read a room-change notice.
lesson.canDo: Identify who was affected by an event and what has been deliberately prepared

grammar.title: An event from the affected person's viewpoint
grammar.formation: Group 1 final u → a + れる (う → われる): 呼ぶ → 呼ばれる. Group 2 drop る + られる: 起こす is Group 1 → 起こされる. する → される; 来る → 来られる. Affected person は actor に passive verb.
grammar.explanation: 森さんに呼ばれました describes being called by Mori. A direct passive need not express annoyance. A suffering passive can make the affected person the subject even if the event was not done directly to them: 雨に降られました means being inconvenienced by rain. With another person's object-related action, retain the object with を: 隣の人に電気を消されました. Context, not the passive ending alone, establishes inconvenience. Some られる forms also express potential or respect; use the actor and situation to interpret them.
grammar.example: 森さんに呼ばれました。

examples.ja: {森|もり}さんに{呼|よ}ばれました。
{弟|おとうと}に{起|お}こされました。
examples.en: I was woken by my younger brother.

examples.ja: {隣|となり}の{人|ひと}に{電気|でんき}を{消|け}されて、{困|こま}りました。
examples.en: The person next to me turned off the light, which caused me trouble.

grammar.mistake: 呼ぶ → 呼ばれる, not 呼ぶられる. Passive does not automatically mean the speaker was angry; do not infer annoyance from a neutral report of being called.

grammar.title: A deliberately prepared state; an event during an interval
grammar.formation: Transitive verb て-form + ある; the prepared object commonly takes が. Verb plain form + 間に; noun + の間に; な-adjective + な間に. い-adjective final い → く + する; な-adjective + にする.
grammar.explanation: 資料が置いてあります points to materials deliberately placed and left ready. It differs from simply describing where someone is or the automatic state of a door. 間に places an event or completion within an interval: 会議の間に電話がありました. 間 without に can describe an action continuing throughout the interval. 明るくする and 静かにする describe making something bright or quiet, rather than just observing that it is so.
grammar.example: 机に資料が置いてあります。
grammar.translation: The materials have been placed on the desk and are ready there.

examples.ja: ドアに{知|し}らせが{貼|は}ってあります。
examples.en: A notice has been put up on the door.

examples.ja: {会議|かいぎ}の{間|あいだ}に、{電話|でんわ}がありました。
examples.en: There was a phone call during the meeting.

examples.ja: {部屋|へや}を{明|あか}るくしてください。

grammar.mistake: Use 置いてあります for a prepared result; 置きます is an action. Use 静かにする, not 静かくする; 明るくする, not 明るいにする.

grammar.title: What I want someone to do; recognize casual shortening
grammar.formation: Person に verb て-form + ほしい; negative ないでほしい. ている → てる; でいる → でる. ておく → とく; でおく → どく. なければ → なきゃ (an obligation ending may be omitted conversationally).
grammar.explanation: 森さんに確認してほしい says that I want Mori to check, rather than that Mori wants to check. Requests with ほしい can sound direct; do not replace professional requests to senior colleagues mechanically with this pattern. In casual conversation, 読んでる means 読んでいる and 書いとく means 書いておく. In 行かなきゃ, the obligation ending is understood. Learn these as recognition forms; careful notices and senior-directed messages retain complete polite wording.
grammar.example: 担当の人に確認してほしいです。
grammar.translation: I want the person in charge to check.

examples.ja: {担当|たんとう}の{人|ひと}に{確認|かくにん}してほしいです。
examples.en: I want the person in charge to check.

examples.ja: ここで{大|おお}きな{声|こえ}で{話|はな}さないでほしいです。
examples.en: I don't want people to speak loudly here.
I'll write the name in advance (casual contraction).

grammar.mistake: ～てほしい names your desired action by someone else; ～たい names your own desired action. 読んでいる contracts to 読んでる, not 読んでてる.

dialogues.title: The meeting has moved
dialogues.scene: Mori explains a changed meeting room at Aoba Systems. The meeting time remains ten; the room changes from A to B.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {森|もり}さんに{呼|よ}ばれました。{会議室|かいぎしつ}に{変更|へんこう}がありますか。
lines.romaji: Mori-san ni yobaremashita. Kaigishitsu ni henkō ga arimasu ka.
lines.meaning: Mori called me. Is there a change to the meeting room?

lines.speaker: Mori
lines.line: はい。{会議|かいぎ}は{十時|じゅうじ}のままですが、{部屋|へや}はBです。
lines.romaji: Hai. Kaigi wa jūji no mama desu ga, heya wa bī desu.
lines.meaning: Yes. The meeting is still at ten, but the room is B.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {資料|しりょう}はどこですか。{受付|うけつけ}で{受|う}け{取|と}りますか。
lines.romaji: Shiryō wa doko desu ka. Uketsuke de uketorimasu ka.
lines.meaning: Where are the materials? Do I collect them at reception?

lines.speaker: Mori
lines.line: Bの{机|つくえ}に{置|お}いてあります。ドアに{案内|あんない}も{貼|は}ってあります。ご{覧|らん}ください。
lines.romaji: Bī no tsukue ni oite arimasu. Doa ni annai mo hatte arimasu. Goran kudasai.
lines.meaning: They've been placed on the desk in B. Information is also posted on the door. Please look at it.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {拝見|はいけん}します。{資料|しりょう}の{担当|たんとう}は{森|もり}さんですね。
lines.romaji: Haiken shimasu. Shiryō no tantō wa Mori-san desu ne.
lines.meaning: I'll look at it. You're the person responsible for the materials, aren't you?

lines.speaker: Mori
lines.line: はい。{会議|かいぎ}の{前|まえ}に、{自分|じぶん}の{連絡先|れんらくさき}を{書|か}いてください。
lines.romaji: Hai. Kaigi no mae ni, jibun no renrakusaki o kaite kudasai.
lines.meaning: Yes. Before the meeting, write your own contact details.

dialogues.title: A call during the meeting
dialogues.scene: After the meeting, you and Mori discuss a telephone call. Mori took the call; the guest is still at reception.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: {会議|かいぎ}の{間|あいだ}に、{電話|でんわ}がありましたか。
lines.romaji: Kaigi no aida ni, denwa ga arimashita ka.
lines.meaning: Was there a call during the meeting?

lines.speaker: Mori
lines.line: はい。{私|わたし}が{出|で}ました。{客|きゃく}は{受付|うけつけ}で{待|ま}っています。
lines.romaji: Hai. Watashi ga demashita. Kyaku wa uketsuke de matte imasu.
lines.meaning: Yes. I answered it. The guest is waiting at reception.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: ご{用件|ようけん}は{何|なん}ですか。{連絡先|れんらくさき}も{確認|かくにん}したいです。
lines.romaji: Goyōken wa nan desu ka. Renrakusaki mo kakunin shitai desu.
lines.meaning: What do they need? I'd also like to check their contact details.

lines.speaker: Mori
lines.line: {資料|しりょう}を{受|う}け{取|と}りたいそうです。{先|さき}に{状況|じょうきょう}を{伝|つた}えてください。
lines.romaji: Shiryō o uketoritai sō desu. Saki ni jōkyō o tsutaete kudasai.
lines.meaning: They say they want to collect the materials. First explain the situation.

lines.speaker: You
lines.line: わかりました。{部屋|へや}を{明|あか}るくしてから、{受付|うけつけ}に{行|い}きます。
lines.romaji: Wakarimashita. Heya o akaruku shite kara, uketsuke ni ikimasu.
lines.meaning: Understood. I'll make the room brighter, then go to reception.

lines.speaker: Mori
lines.line: お{願|ねが}いします。{電気|でんき}は{消|け}さないでください。
lines.romaji: Onegai shimasu. Denki wa kesanaide kudasai.
lines.meaning: Please do. Please don't turn off the light.

{時間|じかん}は{十時|じゅうじ}のままです。

Bの{机|つくえ}に{資料|しりょう}が{置|お}いてあります。
ドアにも{案内|あんない}が{貼|は}ってあります。
{資料|しりょう}に{自分|じぶん}の{連絡先|れんらくさき}を{書|か}いてください。

しずかにしてください

options: The room, from A to B
The time, from ten to noon
The materials contact, from Mori to Satō
exercises.explain: Mori keeps the time at ten and names room B.

exercises.prompt: Where have the materials been prepared?
exercises.explain: Bの机に置いてあります states their prepared location.
Mori says 私が出ました in Mori's own turn.

exercises.context: While you were reading, a person next to you turned off the light and inconvenienced you. Choose the suffering-passive description from your viewpoint.
exercises.line: {隣|となり}の{人|ひと}に{電気|でんき}を＿＿、{困|こま}りました。
exercises.explain: 消されて is the passive of the transitive 消す. 電気 remains the を-marked affected object; the person acting takes に. 困りました supplies the adverse effect.

exercises.context: Mori called you. Report that event from your viewpoint; Mori is the actor.
exercises.explain: 呼ばれました makes you the called person and Mori the に-marked actor.

exercises.context: Describe a notice that someone intentionally posted and left ready on the door.
exercises.line: ドアに{知|し}らせが{貼|は}って＿＿。
exercises.explain: 貼ってあります presents a deliberate resulting state.

exercises.context: Ask someone to make the room brighter.
exercises.explain: い-adjective → く + する: 明るくする.

exercises.context: Say you want the person in charge to check. You are describing your wish, not giving a senior a polite request.
exercises.line: {担当|たんとう}の{人|ひと}に{確認|かくにん}して＿＿です。
exercises.explain: てほしい expresses a desired action by the に-marked person.

exercises.line: {会議|かいぎ}は{中止|ちゅうし}ですか。
exercises.context: The meeting still happens at ten in B. Correct the cancellation assumption.
options: いいえ。{十時|じゅうじ}にBであります。
はい、{会議|かいぎ}はありません。
はい、{時間|じかん}は{十二時|じゅうにじ}です。
exercises.explain: The first reply denies cancellation and retains the stated time and room.

exercises.line: {資料|しりょう}はどこですか。
exercises.context: You placed the materials on the desk and left them there. Report that prepared state.
options: {机|つくえ}に{置|お}いてあります。
まだ{置|お}いていません。
{客|きゃく}が{読|よ}んでいます。
exercises.explain: 置いてあります matches both the deliberate preparation and location.

exercises.meaning: There was a phone call during the meeting.
exercises.explain: 間に locates the event within the meeting interval.

exercises.context: Kenta casually says he will write the notice in advance. Recognize the contraction of 書いておく; this is not a formal office notice.
exercises.prompt: Which casual line means 'I'll write the notice in advance'?
exercises.line: {知|し}らせを{書|か}いておくね。
exercises.explain: 書いとく = 書いておく; 書いてる is currently writing, and 書かなきゃ is must write.

exercises.prompt: Which room should the reader enter?
exercises.explain: AではなくB explicitly contrasts the rooms.
時間は十時のまま; the meeting has not been cancelled.

exercises.prompt: What should readers write on the materials?
exercises.explain: 自分の連絡先 specifies the reader's own details.

exercises.prompt: Who should readers contact if they have a question?
exercises.explain: 森に連絡してください explicitly names the contact.

grammar: てる / とく / なきゃ
watch.prompt: Optionally save five lines from your own media. Separate a passive event from a deliberate prepared state; expand any contracted endings. Do not label every passive as anger or suffering.
